signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Divergent Real Rates
signals.text: CHF/JPY trades at 191.49, outperforming across G10 currency strength scorecards as the Swiss franc leads peers with a 1W average of +0.438% across six pairs while the Japanese yen lags at -0.861% across seven pairs, generating a bilateral spread of 1.299%. SNB policy rate sits at 0.00% with an inflation expectation of 1.24% and a resulting real rate of -1.24%, while the BoJ policy rate is 1.25% with an inflation expectation of 2.70% and a real rate of -1.45%. The SNB zero-rate stance contrasts with the SNB-BoJ carry differential of -125bp favoring the yen, yet fair-value models indicate CHF/JPY at 190.83 is cheap relative to its model fair value of 196.20 with a z-score of -1.68σ. Trade bias: Long CHF/JPY; persistent franc strength against a weak yen supports continued bilateral outperformance. Catalyst: Swiss National Bank policy meeting on 24 Sep with SNB on hold at 0.00%. Risk: Rapid unwinding of cross-currency carry trades compresses the spread below the 0.80% threshold.

signals.title: GBP/USD — CB Divergence + Moving Average Cluster
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3396, positioned below the SMA20 at 1.3519, the SMA50 at 1.3482, and the SMA200 at 1.3455. Fed holds at 4.00%. British pound speculative positioning stands at +18,698 contracts, placing it at the 60th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of +0.28, while 25-day risk reversals show a mild put skew at -0.42. The Bank of England left rates unchanged at its September meeting while signaling an insurance hike in November, providing little immediate support to sterling as economic surprise index reads +5.3. Trade bias: Neutral to bearish GBP/USD; moving average overhead resistance caps near-term recovery attempts. Catalyst: United Kingdom S&P Global PMIs on 22 Sep. Risk: UK PMI prints significantly above consensus expectations and narrows yield spreads in favor of sterling.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Carry Premium
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7140, trading below the SMA20 at 0.7168 but holding above the SMA50 at 0.7087 and the SMA200 at 0.7015. RBA holds at 4.35%. Speculative positioning shows leveraged funds net long +59,299 contracts, reaching the 97th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of +2.11 and weekly additions of +10,920 contracts, while retail sentiment registers 48% long and 52% short. The economic surprise index reads +14.2 alongside a strong inflation expectation of 3.50% and a real policy rate of +0.85%, confirming a mildly restrictive policy stance. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; carry advantage and positive economic data sustain momentum despite extreme positioning. Catalyst: RBA policy meeting on 29 Sep with AONIA at 4.3500% and a hold expected. Risk: Extreme speculative long positioning unwinds sharply if external commodity demand softens.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Options Complacency + Neutral Positioning
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5737, remaining below the SMA20 at 0.5854, the SMA50 at 0.5856, and the SMA200 at 0.5856. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand holds its policy rate at 2.75% with OCR-overnight at 2.7500% compared to the Federal Reserve SOFR at 3.8500%, maintaining a 125bp carry advantage for the US dollar. Speculative positioning sits at -2,319 contracts, representing the 44th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of -0.08, while retail sentiment shows an extreme 87% long against 13% short, creating a clear divergence between institutional and retail participants. The economic surprise index registers +4.2 with inflation expectations at 2.34% and a real policy rate of +0.41%. Trade bias: Neutral NZD/USD; range-bound technical structure with retail long extremes warning of potential mean reversion. Catalyst: New Zealand Westpac McDermott Miller Consumer Confidence survey. Risk: Retail long participants capitulate and spark a deeper break below the 0.5700 support level.
